items.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Critical unauthenticated root RCE in Cisco Expressway Series requires immediate software patching.
items.summary: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series devices allows unauthenticated, remote attackers with network access to execute arbitrary OS commands as root. The flaw stems from the use of persistent cookies alongside insufficient client certificate validation when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering. Attackers possessing valid cookies can connect to the database service and invoke specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands to achieve code execution. Cisco has released software updates to address this security advisory, noting that no workarounds are available.
key_facts: Product: Cisco Expressway Series (Expressway-C and Expressway-E)
Impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution as root
items.bottom_line: Apply Cisco's software updates immediately to prevent unauthenticated remote root command execution on Expressway devices.

claims.text: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root .

items.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8
items.one_liner: Critical security patches for GitLab CE and EE fix multiple high-severity vulnerabilities, including CI/CD and LLM prompt flaws.
items.summary: GitLab has released versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 for Community and Enterprise Editions to address multiple security vulnerabilities and bugs. Notable fixes include a critical integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler, high-severity cross-site scripting, and improper authorization issues. Self-managed installations are strongly urged to upgrade immediately, while GitLab.com and Dedicated tenants have already been patched. The security advisory details various flaws spanning authorization bypasses, regular expression issues, and LLM prompt neutralization failures.

items.bottom_line: Self-managed GitLab installations must be upgraded immediately to address critical and high-severity security flaws.

items.title: Capcom Data Breach Exposes 11.7 Million Email Addresses
items.one_liner: Capcom disclosed a data breach exposing 11.7 million email addresses and account details following unauthorized access to its CAPCOM ID service.
items.summary: Capcom disclosed a data breach affecting its online membership service CAPCOM ID, exposing 11,774,247 email addresses and account details worldwide. Attackers accessed the service on October 19, stealing registration information including creation dates, login counts, and IP addresses, alongside birth dates and countries for a small subset of users. Additionally, unauthorized password changes were executed on 196 accounts, prompting Capcom to reset credentials and establish an incident response task force.
items.bottom_line: Capcom suffered a data breach exposing 11,774,247 email addresses and account details via unauthorized access to its CAPCOM ID service.

items.title: BlackX UEFI Bootkit Bypasses Secure Boot on Patched Windows Systems Missing Revocations
items.one_liner: APT41 is using the BlackX UEFI bootkit to target Central Asian diplomats by exploiting unrevoked Baton Drop vulnerabilities.
items.summary: A sophisticated UEFI bootkit dubbed BlackX has been deployed against diplomatic entities in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan, orchestrated by the China-linked APT41 group. The malware is an updated version of BlackLotus and exploits the patched Secure Boot bypass vulnerability CVE-2022-21894 (Baton Drop) to load malicious code before the OS starts. Complete mitigation requires manually adding the expired Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate to the Secure Boot UEFI Forbidden List (DBX), a step many organizations have neglected. Attackers leverage existing administrator or physical access to drop an RC4-encrypted installer and extensionless payload, subsequently installing Machine Owner Keys to execute arbitrary EFI files.
items.bottom_line: Organizations must manually block the expired Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate in the UEFI DBX list, as attackers continue abusing the Baton Drop vulnerability on patched systems.

items.title: Microsoft pins ConnectWise supply-chain attack to China-state aligned threat group
items.one_liner: Chinese threat group Storm-0940 used AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to target ConnectWise Microsoft 365 environments.
items.summary: Microsoft attributed a supply-chain attack against ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers to the China-state aligned threat group Storm-0940. Using the AI-driven penetration testing framework ARTEX, the threat actor executed automated password-spray attacks reaching 2,900 attempts per minute, before compromising downstream Microsoft 365 environments. The attackers abused OAuth applications and modified credentials to maintain persistence, prompting ConnectWise to temporarily suspend and phase-restore its services.
key_facts: Targeted accounts: 327 Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online accounts across 8 organizations
items.bottom_line: Storm-0940 compromised ConnectWise M365 environments using the AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to automate password spraying and persistence.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets
items.one_liner: A supply chain attack on LiteLLM version 1.107.0 deployed an infostealer and RAT, requiring immediate credential revocation for affected environments.
items.summary: Threat actors compromised LiteLLM's release pipeline, distributing a malicious version (1.107.0) via PyPI and Docker registries that contained an infostealer and a remote access trojan (RAT). The malicious package automatically executes via Python invocation to harvest cloud credentials, browser cookies, and API keys for AI and cloud services. PyPI and Docker removed the compromised images, but organizations that ran version 1.107.0 must treat all cached secrets and environment tokens as compromised.
items.bottom_line: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 contained malicious infostealer and RAT payloads that harvested cloud credentials and API keys upon execution.

items.title: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 - Day Two Results
items.one_liner: Pwn2Own Ireland Day Two featured successful exploits against Home Assistant Green, AI infrastructure, and the Samsung Galaxy S26.
items.summary: On day two of Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, researchers targeted various connected devices, printers, and AI infrastructure platforms across multiple rounds. Notable wins included Yves Bieri taking down Home Assistant Green for $30,000, HaeJung Yang successfully hacking Dynamo in the AI infrastructure category for $40,000, and Taisic Yun breaching the Oracle Autonomous AI Database using unique zero-days and collisions. Meanwhile, attempts against Samsung's Galaxy S26 by a team utilizing Djini.ai succeeded via a confused deputy bug, while printer targets like the Brother MFC-L8970CDW proved challenging.

items.title: [oss-security][CVE-2026-115557] Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in Python ssl module
items.one_liner: Python's ssl module now automatically rejects known compromised certificates via a built-in denylist.
items.summary: Python has added a denylist for compromised intermediate certificates directly into the ssl module via CVE-2026-115557. This change ensures that known compromised certificates are automatically rejected regardless of the configured SSLContext policy. The security update aims to protect users from compromised certificates even if proper certificate revocation checking is absent.

items.title: CVE-2026-114045 (HIGH 8.7): FreeRDP before 3.32.1 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in the server-side rdpsnd channel because an inte…
items.one_liner: FreeRDP before 3.32.1 suffers from an 8.7-rated server-side heap overflow in the audio channel, enabling potential RCE.
items.summary: FreeRDP versions before 3.32.1 contain a heap-based buffer overflow in the server-side rdpsnd channel due to an integer wraparound in rdpsnd_server_select_format() DVI_ADPCM block-alignment arithmetic that bypasses input validation. Malicious RDP clients can exploit this by sending two SNDC_FORMATS PDUs with mismatched block alignments and channel counts, triggering an unbounded heap write during server audio playback. This flaw carries a CVSS base score of 8.7 and can potentially lead to remote code execution.
items.bottom_line: Update FreeRDP to version 3.32.1 or later to mitigate the server-side heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the rdpsnd channel.

items.title: CVE-2026-114084 (HIGH 8.3): Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the /realtime/v1/runs endpoint, which con…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-114084 gives authenticated users SQL injection access to cross-tenant task run data in self-hosted Trigger.dev instances.
items.summary: Trigger.dev versions prior to 4.5.6 contain an SQL injection vulnerability in the /realtime/v1/runs endpoint (CVE-2026-114084) with a CVSS base score of 8.3. The flaw occurs due to unescaped concatenation of the tags query parameter into ElectricSQL clauses, bypassing the runtimeEnvironmentId tenant guard. Authenticated attackers holding project API keys with read:runs scope can append boolean conditions to extract task run payloads and metadata across organizations on the same self-hosted instance.
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-114084 is an 8.3-rated SQL injection vulnerability in Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 that allows unauthorized data extraction across self-hosted instances.

items.summary: A vulnerability in the control channel socket implementation of Open Source Snort 3 allows authenticated, low-privileged local users to execute arbitrary commands and read or write process memory as the Snort 3 process user. items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: HIGH)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks has issued security guidance and mitigation steps for PAN-OS products exposed to critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. CVE-2026-109618 involves uninitialized request memory caused by improper control flow handling during out-of-memory errors via longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. While specific PAN-OS versions are affected, patches are in development, and cloud services like Cortex XCORE and WildFire Cloud have already received remediation patches. Customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions are advised to enable specific Threat IDs to protect against exploitation until official firmware updates are released.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: PHP OOM remote code execution
CVE-2026-109619: PHP longjmp global memory corruption RCE
items.bottom_line: Palo Alto Networks products running vulnerable PHP components face RCE risks from CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, requiring threat prevention signatures or upcoming firmware patches.

items.title: Multiple Cisco Products Snort 3 Visual Basic for Applications Buffer Overflow Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A stack overflow in Cisco's Snort 3 VBA decompression engine lets remote attackers cause a denial of service.
items.summary: Multiple Cisco products contain a vulnerability in the Snort 3 Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) Decompression Engine due to improper range checking. Cisco has released software updates and provided workarounds to address the vulnerability.

items.title: CVE-2026-114081 (HIGH 8.3): Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the TSQL query compiler, which concatenat…
items.one_liner: A high-severity SQL injection vulnerability in Trigger.dev allows authenticated users to exfiltrate other tenants' analytics data via crafted TSQL compiler inputs.
items.summary: Trigger.dev prior to version 4.5.6 suffers from an SQL injection vulnerability located within its TSQL query compiler. The compiler improperly concatenates window-function names into generated ClickHouse SQL without implementing appropriate escaping or allowlisting. Consequently, authenticated customers can submit specially crafted backtick-quoted identifiers to the /api/v1/query endpoint, allowing them to inject raw subqueries that bypass per-tenant WHERE guards. This flaw enables the exfiltration of sensitive analytics data belonging to other organizations. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.3 and was officially published on October 21, 2026.
key_facts: Vulnerability: SQL injection in TSQL query compiler
items.bottom_line: Organizations running Trigger.dev versions prior to 4.5.6 must update immediately to prevent authenticated multi-tenant data exfiltration via the query compiler.

items.title: CVE-2026-0322 PAN-OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) in the Management Interface (Severity: HIGH)
items.one_liner: Audit and restrict PAN-OS management interfaces to internal IP addresses or jump boxes to mitigate CVE-2026-0322.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks disclosed CVE-2026-0322, an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the management interface of PAN-OS software affecting PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. The flaw enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges. Palo Alto Networks rated the severity HIGH with a CVSS base score of 8.6, noting very limited exploitation targeting management interfaces exposed to the internet. Customers are advised to restrict management access to trusted internal IP addresses or jump boxes, and Threat Prevention subscribers can enable Threat IDs 510046 and 510047 for limited signature coverage.

items.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
items.one_liner: Using terminal database checks as reinforcement learning rewards significantly improves AI agent reliability and repeatable success on complex tasks.
items.summary: Researchers have developed ThinkingBox, a framework that evaluates AI agent performance by comparing terminal database states against expected outcomes. By treating these executable database checks as reward functions, the team fine-tuned the Qwen3.8-27B model using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) over 50 steps. The approach significantly boosted repeatable success rates on complex agentic tasks outside the standard benchmark by filtering out hopeless or already-solved training scenarios using offline policy-relative difficulty.
items.bottom_line: Turning executable database checks into post-training RL rewards sharply increases reliable task completion for large language model agents.

items.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale
items.one_liner: NVIDIA OpenShell provides an open-source runtime architecture using hardware-enforced isolation, gateways, and policy provers to secure autonomous AI agent workloads.
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents operating over extended horizons face compounding security risks as they dynamically download code, build tools, and access infrastructure without intrinsic safety priorities. To address this, NVIDIA OpenShell provides an open-source runtime architecture that treats agent workloads as untrusted and enforces strict security controls at the infrastructure level. OpenShell consists of four primary components: a Gateway control plane for sandboxes, a Supervisor to mediate network and credential access, an isolated Sandbox environment, and a Policy Prover for formal verification. Running on NVIDIA Vera CPUs, the architecture ensures high-performance computing while guaranteeing that agent actions remain strictly bounded by organizational policies.
key_facts: Core Components: Gateway, Supervisor, Sandbox, Policy prover
items.bottom_line: Securing autonomous AI agents requires moving governance out of the agent and into an infrastructure runtime that isolates execution and verifies action policies.

items.title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
items.one_liner: Ruby patched three Onigmo regex engine memory corruption bugs that enabled four critical RCE flaws in GitLab.
items.summary: Ruby released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 to fix three Onigmo regular expression engine bugs that caused four critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in GitLab. The bugs allow specially crafted patterns compiled from untrusted input via Regexp.new, interpolation, or similar methods to corrupt memory. GitLab patched four CVEs—including two maximum-severity 10.0 scores (CVE-2026-97229 and CVE-2026-110264)—by updating its embedded Ruby runtimes. Administrators of self-managed GitLab instances must upgrade to the latest security releases, as standard defenses like setting regex timeouts or capping pattern lengths are ineffective.
key_facts: Affected component: Onigmo regular expression engine
items.bottom_line: Applications compiling regexes from untrusted input are vulnerable to memory corruption via Onigmo engine bugs and must update Ruby immediately.

items.title: Microsoft Links ConnectWise Breach to China-Linked Group Using AI Pentesting Tool ARTEX
items.one_liner: Threat actor Storm-0940 leveraged an AI pentesting tool called ARTEX to rapidly exploit stolen ConnectWise credentials and compromise Microsoft 365 tenants.
items.summary: China-linked state-sponsored group Storm-0940 targeted 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants by exploiting stolen ConnectWise credentials at machine speed. The attackers utilized ARTEX, an open-source AI-driven penetration testing framework, to accelerate compromise, achieving privileged access to cloud infrastructure in under three hours in several instances. Before using the stolen ConnectWise credentials, the group executed password spraying attacks from IP address 144.172.64.99, generating over 151,000 failed login attempts. Following successful authentication via existing application permissions, the AI agents conducted directory reconnaissance, modified application credentials for persistence, and attempted role modifications. Microsoft advises defenders to review all service principal credential additions dating back to at least October 1 to remove potential backdoors.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are using AI frameworks like ARTEX to automate credential abuse and establish persistent backdoors in cloud environments within hours of a supply chain breach.

items.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
items.one_liner: Two CVSS 9.0 KSMBD RCE flaws were publicly dumped via AI scanning reports without upstream patches, leaving Linux servers exposed.
items.summary: Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, face two remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative that were disclosed publicly without prior mainline kernel fixes. The first flaw, ZDI-CAN-33549, is an integer underflow requiring SMB Direct, an RDMA-capable interface, and a writable share. The second flaw, ZDI-CAN-33774, enables unauthenticated pre-authentication attacks over port 445 due to a handler table assignment race condition. ZDI routed these reports using automated AI scans directly to public mailing lists without attached patches, drawing sharp criticism from stable-kernel maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman. Because the kernel assigns CVEs only after stable-tree fixes are ready, administrators currently lack official patches and must rely on checking if the KSMBD module is active.
key_facts: Affected Component: KSMBD Linux kernel SMB server
items.bottom_line: AI-discovered kernel bugs sent directly to public mailing lists without patches create immediate zero-day risk for administrators before fixes exist.

items.title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
items.one_liner: APT41-linked threat actors revived the BlackLotus bootkit under the name BlackX to target diplomatic agencies in Central Asia via the Baton Drop vulnerability.
items.summary: Security researchers uncovered an APT campaign in early 2026 targeting diplomatic organizations in Central Asian countries—specifically Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan—using a revived UEFI bootkit dubbed BlackX. The malware bears striking similarities to the BlackLotus bootkit advertised on hacking forums in 2022 and confirmed by researchers in 2023. The attackers gained administrator privileges on victim machines before deploying an RC4-encrypted installer package that exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to install custom Machine Owner Keys (MOK) and bypass Secure Boot. Once executed, the UEFI payload injects a malicious, custom-signed driver into the Windows kernel to establish persistence.
items.bottom_line: Sophisticated threat actors are reviving and adapting advanced UEFI bootkits like BlackLotus to bypass Secure Boot and compromise diplomatic networks in Central Asia.

items.title: SafePay Has Compromised 600 Critical Infrastructure Victims Worldwide, CISA Warns
items.one_liner: SafePay ransomware has hit over 600 critical infrastructure targets globally using extensive initial access vectors and double extortion.
items.summary: The SafePay ransomware group has compromised at least 600 critical infrastructure organizations across North America, South America, Europe, and Australia since emerging in August 2024. A joint advisory from US, German, and UK agencies highlights SafePay's extensive initial access vectors, including credential exposure, brute-force attacks, VPN exploitation, and edge device vulnerabilities. The group employs living-off-the-land administrative tools, disables security software, and uses a double extortion model backed by phone calls and a ChaCha20/RSA hybrid encryption scheme. SafePay is believed to be a rebrand of well-known ransomware operations like LockBit, ALPHV/BlackCat, and INC Ransomware.

Encryption: ChaCha20 stream cipher with RSA public-key cryptosystem

items.title: Children’s Data Stolen After Ransomware Attack Compromises ‘Password1’ Account
items.one_liner: A simple 'Password1' credential on a forgotten test account led to a significant data breach of children's records, highlighting the critical need for basic identity and access hygiene.
items.summary: A ransomware attack on Data Cymru, a Welsh government-funded data unit, compromised the personal information of 3,300 people, primarily children. Attackers gained initial access through a 12-year-old test account protected only by the password 'Password1'. The breach resulted in the exfiltration of 42GB of data and the encryption of 182.7GB of files. The UK's Information Commissioner’s Office issued a reprimand to both Data Cymru and its IT provider, Ogi Networks Limited, for significant security failures, though no financial penalties were imposed.
items.bottom_line: Neglecting to audit and secure legacy test accounts with MFA and strong credentials remains a primary vector for catastrophic data exfiltration.

items.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web

items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) confirmed an incident involving the loss of certain data after 3,897 customer records containing personal information were found within a dark web dataset of roughly 375,000 records. The exposed data includes customer names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, and internal CIF identifiers, though sensitive financial details like account balances and passwords were not listed. The leak was flagged to the bank on October 16 by CERT-In and the Defense Cyber Agency, prompting SBI to engage an independent cybersecurity auditor. While the bank noted no material impact on core operations, the exposed details pose severe impersonation and phishing risks to customers.

items.title: How verification enables smarter model routing for AI coding
items.one_liner: Stop routing all code to frontier models; you need to account for security and maintainability debt, not just cost and latency.
items.summary: Sonar Research argues that AI model routing should be treated as a quality control mechanism rather than just a cost-saving lever. Current routing strategies often flatten performance into a single metric, ignoring critical dimensions like security, functional correctness, reliability, and maintainability. Research shows that models diverge significantly in these areas, with some producing higher rates of security debt or runtime defects despite similar aggregate benchmarks. The industry is encouraged to match model capability to the specific criticality of the task, such as using frontier models for security-sensitive code while utilizing lower-tier models for routine work.
items.bottom_line: Effective AI coding strategy requires routing tasks based on specific quality dimensions like security and reliability rather than defaulting to the most expensive model.

claims.text: The industry has decided routing is a cost lever, but the empirical case for treating it as a quality control is at least as strong.

items.one_liner: A critical memory allocation vulnerability in Web::Simple allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger excessive memory usage via crafted Content-Length headers.
items.summary: Web::Simple versions before 0.035 for Perl are vulnerable to a memory allocation issue where the application allocates a buffer based on the Content-Length header provided in a request. An attacker can trigger this by sending a crafted request with a Content-Length value significantly larger than the actual body, leading to excessive memory consumption. This vulnerability affects routes that match body parameters and does not require authentication to exploit. items.title: USN-8951-1: c-ares vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Multiple denial of service and memory allocation vulnerabilities in c-ares impact multiple Ubuntu LTS versions.
items.summary: Several vulnerabilities have been identified in c-ares, an asynchronous DNS client library, affecting various Ubuntu releases. items.one_liner: GhostLock (CVE-2026-43499) was successfully ported to root a bootloader-locked Unisoc T8300 Android 16 device without modifying the boot image.
items.summary: A security researcher successfully rooted a bootloader-locked Redmi A7 Pro 5G running Android 16 and a Unisoc T8300 processor without flashing the boot image or unlocking the bootloader. The exploit leveraged the public GhostLock vulnerability (CVE-2026-43499), a futex priority-inheritance stack use-after-free bug in Linux kernel 6.6. The primary technical hurdle involved deriving the physical load address (P0), which changes on every boot via TrustZone and KASLR seeds. By utilizing a tracefs leak to uncover the virtual slide and physical offset, the author achieved a uid-0 kernel credential patch from an authorized ADB shell across multiple boots.
key_facts: Target device: Redmi A7 Pro 5G (Unisoc T8300)
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-43499 enables per-boot root access on locked Unisoc Android 16 devices by dynamically resolving per-boot physical load addresses.

items.summary: A path traversal vulnerability in Postiz, tracked as CVE-2026-115932, allows registered users to read arbitrary server files by supplying a crafted media path. items.title: CVE-2026-116019 - Grav 2.0.15 before 2.2.13 Allowlist Bypass via Flex Form Override Directives
items.one_liner: Review CMS access controls and patch Grav to prevent authenticated arbitrary file deletion and reading via Flex form overrides.
items.summary: Grav versions 2.0.15 up to 2.2.13 are vulnerable to an allowlist bypass via Flex Form override directives, tracked as CVE-2026-116019. The flaw allows page editors to invoke arbitrary public static methods by relocating data-*@ directives with unset-name@ or integer keys. Attackers possessing page-edit permissions can embed crafted fields inside Flex form overrides within page frontmatter to execute sensitive functions like Folder::delete or Utils::download. This exploitation vector enables malicious actors to delete directories, overwrite files, or read arbitrary files outside the designated page tree.
key_facts: Affected component: Flex Form override directives
items.bottom_line: Page editors on vulnerable Grav installations can execute arbitrary public static methods and manipulate files outside the page tree.

items.summary: IO::Compress::Brotli versions from 0.004001 before 0.023 for Perl bundle a vulnerable copy of the Brotli library that suffers from an out-of-bounds write in the decoder. items.title: Why AI Can’t Replace Engineering Teams
items.one_liner: Engineers must push back against the misconception that AI demos can replace production engineering teams.
items.summary: Generative AI tools and demos create an illusion among corporate leadership that software engineering is simple, leading to misplaced beliefs that AI can entirely replace engineering teams. Rather than chasing every shiny AI object, engineers must remain focused on building safe and useful products for human users.
items.bottom_line: Corporate leadership must recognize that working AI code demos do not replace the complex architecture and compliance work handled by real engineering teams.

items.bottom_line: Conventional AppSec scanners fail to catch prompt-based threats in AI agent skills and packages, leaving workflows vulnerable to sophisticated evasion techniques.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: Encryption isn’t enough to protect data wherever it goes
items.one_liner: Vaultless, keyless pseudonymization protects data across cloud and AI workflows by replacing sensitive values with realistic substitutes, removing central vaults as single points of failure.
items.summary: Traditional cybersecurity policies rely on database encryption, network security, and access controls, but fail to protect data once decrypted and processed across cloud platforms, analytics tools, and AI pipelines. Because data must be read to be used, breaches or future quantum decryption can expose sensitive plaintext information. To mitigate this risk without stalling operations, policymakers and organizations are turning to vaultless, keyless pseudonymization. This approach replaces sensitive identifiers like names, social security numbers, and payment cards with structurally valid substitutes, eliminating central vaults as single points of failure and rendering stolen data useless to threat actors.
items.bottom_line: Encryption leaves decrypted data vulnerable during processing, making vaultless pseudonymization necessary to strip stolen data of its value.

claims.text: Encryption protects data when it is stored or traveling, only partially protects it when it is transmitted, and does not protect data at all when it is processed.
claims.support_span: Encryption protects data when it is stored or traveling, only partially protects it when it is transmitted, and does not protect data at all when it is processed.

items.title: LLM-Jailbreaks erklärt: Angriffe auf der Prompt-Ebene, keine Bugs
items.one_liner: Jailbreaks are prompt-level exploits that cannot be 'fixed' in the model weights, requiring a shift toward system-level security and monitoring.
items.summary: Research into LLM jailbreaks demonstrates that these attacks are prompt-level manipulations rather than model defects, meaning they cannot be permanently patched through fine-tuning or weight adjustments. A study using 32 malicious prompts showed that attackers can achieve near-perfect success rates by selecting the most effective attack strategy for a given model. Because the space of possible prompts is open-ended, security teams must focus on measuring attack success rates against specific model versions rather than seeking a universal fix. The research highlights that jailbreaks are an inherent property of how models are instructed to follow conflicting directives.
key_facts: Study: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail? (arXiv 2307.02483)
items.bottom_line: Stop treating jailbreaks as bugs to be patched and start treating them as an inevitable, ongoing risk that requires robust input validation and output monitoring.

items.summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. items.title: A distant Pacific phenomenon may be drying India’s north, says study
items.one_liner: A study links a North Pacific oceanic phenomenon called the Victoria Mode to drying climates and shifting weather zones across northern India.
items.summary: A study by researchers at the India Meteorological Department and IITM published in MAUSAM reveals that climatic zones across India are shifting due to a North Pacific oceanic pattern known as the 'Victoria Mode' (VM). The negative phase of the VM reduces moisture inflow, causing the hot semi-arid steppe zone in north-west India to expand from 25.7% to 33.1% between 1951-2020 while drying northern regions like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Researchers warn that these long-term zone contractions pose serious risks to food safety and population displacement.

items.summary: MemT-1.0 is a new generation of memory foundation models that makes persistent, dynamically evolving memory an intrinsic part of model computation. MemT-1.0 integrates dynamic local memory and trainable hyper memory to retain and leverage historical information without accessing original context at inference. Its persistent state remains constant in size, reducing storage by approximately 66× versus full-context KV cache at 128K history length. The project makes three main contributions: - Memory architecture. Introduce MemT-1.0 with improved memory storage and utilization, and Mixture-of-Storage (MoS) for scalable memory capacity.
